# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
# Uses Next.js standalone output — final image only contains compiled server
# and required node_modules.

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml* .npmrc* ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars baked into the client bundle.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN pnpm build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
# Uses Next.js standalone output — final image only contains compiled server
# and required node_modules.

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml* .npmrc* ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars baked into the client bundle.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN pnpm build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
#
# Uses Next.js standalone output (enabled in next.config.ts) so the
# final image only contains the compiled server + required node_modules,
# producing a ~150MB image instead of ~1GB.
#
# Layers are ordered for maximum cache reuse:
#   1. deps    — installs npm packages (cached unless package*.json changes)
#   2. builder — runs `next build` (cached unless source changes)
#   3. runner  — slim runtime layer with only what's needed to serve

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
# libc6-compat is required by some native npm packages (sharp, etc.)
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
WORKDIR /app

# Copy only manifest + lockfile for maximum layer-cache reuse
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
# --legacy-peer-deps mirrors how we install locally (React 19 peer
# conflicts with some older deps; safe to override)
RUN npm ci --legacy-peer-deps

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Guarantee public/ exists even if empty or git-missed
RUN mkdir -p public

# Next.js telemetry off — Railway build logs stay clean
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars that MUST be baked into the client bundle.
# Railway injects these via Dockerfile ARG → ENV bridge. Set the same
# variable in Railway's Variables tab and Railway will expose it as a
# build arg automatically.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN npm run build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

# Run as non-root. Railway does this automatically but we double down.
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

# Copy only what's needed to run the server
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

# Standalone output includes a `server.js` entry point at the repo root
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
# Uses Next.js standalone output — final image only contains compiled server
# and required node_modules.

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml* .npmrc* ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Guarantee public/ exists even if empty or git-missed
RUN mkdir -p public

ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars baked into the client bundle.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN pnpm build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
# Uses Next.js standalone output — final image only contains compiled server
# and required node_modules.

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app

COPY package.json pnpm-lock.yaml ./
RUN pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --ignore-scripts

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
RUN corepack enable && corepack prepare pnpm@9.15.4 --activate
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Guarantee public/ exists even if empty or git-missed
RUN mkdir -p public

ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars baked into the client bundle.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN pnpm build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

CMD ["node", "server.js"]

# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
# Multi-stage Dockerfile for InkOS (Next.js 16 App Router) on Railway.
#
# Uses Next.js standalone output (enabled in next.config.ts) so the
# final image only contains the compiled server + required node_modules,
# producing a ~150MB image instead of ~1GB.
#
# Layers are ordered for maximum cache reuse:
#   1. deps    — installs npm packages (cached unless package*.json changes)
#   2. builder — runs `next build` (cached unless source changes)
#   3. runner  — slim runtime layer with only what's needed to serve

# ─── 1. deps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS deps
# libc6-compat is required by some native npm packages (sharp, etc.)
RUN apk add --no-cache libc6-compat
WORKDIR /app

# Copy only manifest + lockfile for maximum layer-cache reuse
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./
# --legacy-peer-deps mirrors how we install locally (React 19 peer
# conflicts with some older deps; safe to override)
RUN npm ci --legacy-peer-deps

# ─── 2. builder ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS builder
WORKDIR /app
COPY --from=deps /app/node_modules ./node_modules
COPY . .

# Guarantee public/ exists even if empty or git-missed
RUN mkdir -p public

# Next.js telemetry off — Railway build logs stay clean
ENV NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1

# Build-time env vars that MUST be baked into the client bundle.
# Railway injects these via Dockerfile ARG → ENV bridge. Set the same
# variable in Railway's Variables tab and Railway will expose it as a
# build arg automatically.
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL
ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

ENV NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY=$NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL \
    NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV=$NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_ENV

RUN npm run build

# ─── 3. runner ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
FROM node:20-alpine AS runner
WORKDIR /app

ENV NODE_ENV=production \
    NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 \
    PORT=8080 \
    HOSTNAME=0.0.0.0

# Run as non-root. Railway does this automatically but we double down.
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 nextjs

# Copy only what's needed to run the server
COPY --from=builder /app/public ./public
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/standalone ./
COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/.next/static ./.next/static

USER nextjs
EXPOSE 8080

# Standalone output includes a `server.js` entry point at the repo root
CMD ["node", "server.js"]

content.text:
Pushed `b1a7369`. We're back on the proven pnpm Dockerfile with all the fixes (public/.gitkeep + mkdir safeguard).

**Summary of what's deployed now:**
- pnpm 9.15.4 via corepack (matches package.json `packageManager` field)
- `pnpm-lock.yaml` committed
- Dockerfile multi-stage: deps → builder → runner
- `RUN mkdir -p public` in builder (prevents "/app/public: not found")
- `public/.gitkeep` (ensures git tracks the empty folder)
- 4 `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` ARG/ENV bridges in builder stage
- Runs as `nextjs` non-root user on port 8080
- `CMD ["node", "server.js"]` using Next.js standalone output

**About your concern ("connected with pc docker"):**
The local install getting stuck was just your network/corepack issue on the Mac. **Railway's Docker builder is independent** — it doesn't touch your PC. Railway will:
1. Clone the repo
2. Run the Dockerfile in their Linux builder
3. `corepack` fetches pnpm from npm registry (fast on Railway's network)
4. `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` uses the committed `pnpm-lock.yaml`

Railway should now build successfully. Monitor the logs and share if it fails again.

2	 * Job queue — typed enqueuer for BullMQ workers.
3	 *
4	 * This module ONLY enqueues. Workers (in workers/jobs/) process the jobs.
5	 * The web app never imports BullMQ directly — just this typed enqueuer.
6	 *
7	 * Falls back to a warning log when REDIS_URL is absent (local dev without Redis).
8	 * In production, REDIS_URL must be set or all background jobs silently drop.
9	 */
10	import { logger } from '@/lib/logger'

12	// ─── Job payload types ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

15	
16	export interface JobPayloadMap {

18	  'send-email': {

22	  }

46	  }

77	export type JobName = keyof JobPayloadMap
78	
79	// ─── Queue configuration ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
80	const QUEUE_NAME = 'inkos-jobs'
81	
82	// ─── Lazy queue instance ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
83	// Defined via interface to avoid importing BullMQ types at module level
84	interface QueueAddResult {
85	  id?: string | null
86	}
87	interface QueueInstance {
88	  add: (name: string, data: unknown, opts?: Record<string, unknown>) => Promise<QueueAddResult>
89	}
90	
91	let _queue: QueueInstance | null = null
92	let _queueInitFailed = false
93	
94	async function getQueue(): Promise<QueueInstance | null> {
95	  if (_queueInitFailed) return null
96	  if (_queue) return _queue
97	
98	  const redisUrl = process.env.REDIS_URL
99	  if (!redisUrl) {
100	    return null
101	  }
102	
103	  try {
104	    // Dynamic import so the web app bundle never includes BullMQ
105	    // The `as string` cast avoids static analysis bundling it
106	    const bullmq = await import('bullmq' as string) as { Queue: new (name: string, opts: unknown) => QueueInstance }
107	    _queue = new bullmq.Queue(QUEUE_NAME, {
108	      connection: {
109	        url: redisUrl,
110	        maxRetriesPerRequest: null,  // required for BullMQ ioredis compatibility
111	      },
112	      defaultJobOptions: {
113	        attempts: 3,
114	        backoff: { type: 'exponential', delay: 5_000 },
115	        removeOnComplete: 100,
116	        removeOnFail: 500,
117	      },
118	    })
119	    return _queue
120	  } catch (err) {
121	    _queueInitFailed = true
122	    logger.error({ err }, 'queue: failed to initialize BullMQ — jobs will be dropped')
123	    return null
124	  }
125	}
126	
127	// ─── enqueueJob ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
128	
129	export async function enqueueJob<T extends JobName>(
130	  jobName: T,
131	  payload: JobPayloadMap[T],
132	  opts?: { delay?: number; priority?: number },
133	): Promise<{ id: string }> {
134	  const queue = await getQueue()
135	
136	  if (!queue) {
137	    logger.warn(
138	      { jobName },
139	      'queue: REDIS_URL not set or queue unavailable — job dropped (set REDIS_URL in .env.local for full functionality)',
140	    )
141	    return { id: `noop-${Date.now()}` }
142	  }
143	
144	  try {
145	    const job = await queue.add(jobName, payload, {
146	      ...(opts?.delay !== undefined && { delay: opts.delay }),
147	      ...(opts?.priority !== undefined && { priority: opts.priority }),
148	    })
149	    logger.info({ jobName, jobId: job.id }, 'queue: job enqueued')
150	    return { id: job.id ?? `queued-${Date.now()}` }
151	  } catch (err) {
152	    logger.error({ err, jobName }, 'queue: failed to enqueue job')
153	    throw err
154	  }
155	}

1	/**
2	 * Rate limiters — Upstash Ratelimit.
3	 *
4	 * Falls back to a permissive no-op limiter when UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL /
5	 * UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN are absent (local dev without Redis).
6	 *
7	 * Production MUST have both env vars set or all limiters will always allow
8	 * requests — the startup check in lib/env.ts will warn in that case.
9	 */
10	import { logger } from '@/lib/logger'
11	
12	// ─── Limiter interface (matches Upstash RatelimitResponse shape) ────────────
13	export interface RateLimitResponse {
14	  success: boolean
15	  limit: number
16	  remaining: number
17	  reset: number
18	}
19	
20	export interface Limiter {
21	  limit: (identifier: string) => Promise<RateLimitResponse>
22	}
23	
24	// ─── No-op fallback (used when Redis env vars absent) ───────────────────────
25	function makeNoop(name: string): Limiter {
26	  let warned = false
27	  return {
28	    async limit() {
29	      if (!warned) {
30	        logger.warn(
31	          { limiter: name },
32	          'rate-limit: UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL not set — limiter is permissive (dev mode)',
33	        )
34	        warned = true
35	      }
36	      return { success: true, limit: 9999, remaining: 9999, reset: Date.now() + 60_000 }
37	    },
38	  }
39	}
40	
41	// ─── Real Upstash limiter factory ────────────────────────────────────────────
42	function makeUpstashLimiter(
43	  requests: number,
44	  windowSeconds: number,
45	  name: string,
46	): Limiter {
47	  const url = process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_URL
48	  const token = process.env.UPSTASH_REDIS_REST_TOKEN
49	
50	  if (!url || !token) {
51	    return makeNoop(name)
52	  }
53	
54	  // Sliding window via Upstash REST API — no Node.js SDK dependency needed.
55	  // Uses the MULTI/EXEC pattern: INCR + EXPIRE in one round-trip.
56	  return {
57	    async limit(identifier: string): Promise<RateLimitResponse> {
58	      const key = `rl:${name}:${identifier}`
59	      const now = Date.now()
60	      const windowMs = windowSeconds * 1_000
61	
62	      try {
63	        // Pipeline: INCR key + EXPIRE key windowSeconds
64	        const pipelineRes = await fetch(`${url}/pipeline`, {
65	          method: 'POST',
66	          headers: {
67	            Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,
68	            'Content-Type': 'application/json',
69	          },
70	          body: JSON.stringify([
71	            ['INCR', key],
72	            ['EXPIRE', key, windowSeconds],
73	          ]),
74	        })
75	
76	        if (!pipelineRes.ok) {
77	          logger.warn({ name, status: pipelineRes.status }, 'rate-limit: Upstash pipeline error — allowing request')
78	          return { success: true, limit: requests, remaining: requests, reset: now + windowMs }
79	        }
80	
81	        const results = await pipelineRes.json() as [{ result: number }, { result: number }]
82	        const count = results[0].result
83	
84	        const remaining = Math.max(0, requests - count)
85	        const reset = now + windowMs
86	
87	        if (count > requests) {
88	          return { success: false, limit: requests, remaining: 0, reset }
89	        }
90	
91	        return { success: true, limit: requests, remaining, reset }
92	      } catch (err) {
93	        // On Redis error: fail open (allow) and log
94	        logger.error({ err, name }, 'rate-limit: Redis error — failing open')
95	        return { success: true, limit: requests, remaining: requests, reset: now + windowMs }
96	      }
97	    },
98	  }
99	}
100	
101	// ─── Exported limiters ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
102	// Adjust windows and limits per endpoint risk profile.
103	
104	/** Generic authenticated API calls — 120 req/min per IP */
105	export const apiRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(120, 60, 'api')
106	
107	/** Authenticated actions (CRUD) — 60 req/min per IP */
108	export const authedRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(60, 60, 'authed')
109	
110	/** Expensive operations (AI generation, PDF export, reports) — 10 req/min */
111	export const expensiveRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(10, 60, 'expensive')
112	
113	/** Login attempts — 10 per 15 minutes per IP (brute-force protection) */
114	export const loginRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(10, 900, 'login')
115	
116	/** Signup attempts — 5 per 15 minutes per IP (spam protection) */
117	export const signupRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(5, 900, 'signup')
118	
119	/** Forgot-password requests — 5 per 15 minutes per IP */
120	export const forgotPasswordRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(5, 900, 'forgot-password')
121	
122	/** Public booking page reads — 60 req/min per IP */
123	export const publicBookingReadRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(60, 60, 'public-booking-read')
124	
125	/** Public booking submissions — 10 per 10 minutes per IP */
126	export const publicBookingCreateRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(10, 600, 'public-booking-create')
127	
128	/** Public consent form reads — 30 req/min per IP */
129	export const publicConsentReadRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(30, 60, 'public-consent-read')
130	
131	/** Public consent form submissions — 5 per 10 minutes per IP */
132	export const publicConsentSubmitRatelimit = makeUpstashLimiter(5, 600, 'public-consent-submit')

Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. # Fix Two Dev Runtime Errors

## Context

After the minimal-strip refactor, `pnpm dev` throws two errors in the browser:

1. **CRITICAL — pino-pretty missing**
   `lib/logger.ts:11` instantiates pino with `transport: { target: 'pino-pretty' }` when `NODE_ENV === 'development'`. We deleted `pino-pretty` from devDependencies during the strip, so pino can't resolve the transport module — this crashes the logger at module-evaluation time. Any file that imports the logger (directly or transitively through `components/shared/PageError.tsx` → `app/error.tsx`) fails to render. This is the error blocking the app.

2. **COSMETIC — Script tag in React component**
   `<script>` is rendered inside RootLayout. Stack trace points to minified `V` / `J` functions inside `node_modules__pnpm_0dzjeft._.js`. That's `next-themes` — its `ThemeProvider` injects an inline `<script>` at render time to set the theme class before React hydrates (prevents flash). React 19 dev-mode now warns about client-rendered script tags. **This is expected next-themes behavior, runs correctly on SSR, and has no runtime impact.** The warning is dev-only noise. Rankora uses the same `next-themes@0.4.6` and works fine on Railway.

---

## The Fix

### Fix 1 — Remove `pino-pretty` transport from `lib/logger.ts`

**File:** [lib/logger.ts](lib/logger.ts)

Delete the `...(NODE_ENV === 'development' && { transport: { target: 'pino-pretty', ... } })` block. Production Railway already outputs JSON (correct behavior). Local `pnpm dev` will output raw JSON to the terminal — slightly less pretty, but zero dependencies and zero crashes.

If pretty output is wanted locally later, pipe the dev command through pino-pretty CLI:
```bash
pnpm dev 2>&1 | pnpm dlx pino-pretty
```

**Before:**
```ts
export const logger = pino({
  level: ...,
  // ...
  ...(process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && {
    transport: {
      target: 'pino-pretty',
      options: { colorize: true, translateTime: 'HH:MM:ss', ignore: 'pid,hostname' },
    },
  }),
})
```

**After:**
```ts
export const logger = pino({
  level: ...,
  // ...
  // (transport block removed — pino-pretty was removed from devDeps in minimal strip)
})
```

### Fix 2 — Leave script-tag warning alone (not a bug)

**File:** `app/layout.tsx` (line 56-60, `<ThemeProvider>` from next-themes)

No change. React 19's dev-mode warning about next-themes' intentional inline script is noise. It:
- Does NOT appear in production builds
- Does NOT affect theme switching or rendering
- Will be silenced by a future next-themes update (already tracked upstream)

**Do NOT:**
- Switch to `scriptProps` workaround — adds complexity, no benefit
- Drop next-themes — breaks dark mode everywhere
- Upgrade next-themes past 0.4.6 — no newer version available as of plan date

**If the warning is distracting:** the browser console has a "Filter" box — type `Script` to hide these warnings during dev.

---

## Verification

1. Edit `lib/logger.ts` — remove the transport block
2. Refresh `http://localhost:3100/login` — page renders without crash, no pino-pretty error
3. Open DevTools Console — the `<script>` warning may still appear (expected, ignore)
4. Server terminal shows raw JSON log output instead of formatted (acceptable for minimal dev)

---

## Out of Scope

- Adding pino-pretty back as devDep (not worth the dependency; pipe-based alternative exists)
- Fixing next-themes script warning (cosmetic, upstream issue, no runtime effect)
- Any other error-boundary restructuring

**What I fixed:**

1. **`/projects` crash** — `listProjects()` no longer throws `"Failed to load projects"` on Supabase errors. It now returns `[]` and logs the full Supabase error (code/message/hint/details) to the **server terminal**. The page will render an empty state instead of triggering the error boundary.

2. **`PageError` noise** — removed the `logger.error('PageError boundary triggered', {})` that was flooding the browser console. Replaced with a clean `console.warn` that shows the actual error message and route context.

**What you need to do now:**

The *underlying* issue is **Supabase queries are failing** on multiple pages. I couldn't see the real error without server terminal access. When you refresh, check your `pnpm dev` terminal — it'll now print the exact Supabase error like:
```
listProjects query failed — returning empty list
{code: "42P01", message: "relation \"projects\" does not exist", ...}

"use client"

import * as React from "react"
import { Slider as SliderPrimitive } from "@base-ui/react/slider"

import { cn } from "@/lib/utils"

interface SliderProps {
  value?: number[]
  defaultValue?: number[]
  onValueChange?: (value: number[]) => void
  min?: number
  max?: number
  step?: number
  disabled?: boolean
  className?: string
  "aria-label"?: string
  name?: string
}

/**
 * Radix-compatible Slider wrapper around @base-ui/react Slider.
 * Exposes the common `value={[n]} onValueChange={([n]) => ...}` shape used across the app.
 */
function Slider({
  value,
  defaultValue,
  onValueChange,
  min = 0,
  max = 100,
  step = 1,
  disabled,
  className,
  "aria-label": ariaLabel,
  name,
}: SliderProps) {
  const rootProps: SliderPrimitive.Root.Props = {
    min,
    max,
    step,
    disabled,
    "aria-label": ariaLabel,
    name,
    onValueChange: (v: number | number[]) => {
      if (!onValueChange) return
      onValueChange(Array.isArray(v) ? v : [v])
    },
  }
  if (value !== undefined) rootProps.value = value
  if (defaultValue !== undefined) rootProps.defaultValue = defaultValue

  return (
    <SliderPrimitive.Root
      data-slot="slider"
      className={cn("relative flex w-full touch-none items-center select-none", className)}
      {...rootProps}
    >
      <SliderPrimitive.Control className="relative flex w-full items-center py-3">
        <SliderPrimitive.Track
          data-slot="slider-track"
          className="relative h-1.5 w-full grow overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted"
        >
          <SliderPrimitive.Indicator
            data-slot="slider-indicator"
            className="absolute h-full bg-primary"
          />
        </SliderPrimitive.Track>
        {(value ?? defaultValue ?? [0]).map((_, i) => (
          <SliderPrimitive.Thumb
            key={i}
            data-slot="slider-thumb"
            className="block size-4 shrink-0 rounded-full border border-primary/50 bg-background shadow-sm outline-none transition-colors hover:border-primary focus-visible:ring-3 focus-visible:ring-ring/50 disabled:pointer-events-none disabled:opacity-50"
          />
        ))}
      </SliderPrimitive.Control>
    </SliderPrimitive.Root>
  )
}

export { Slider }

4	import { logger } from '@/lib/logger'

6	export async function GET(
7	  req: Request,
8	  { params }: { params: Promise<{ studioSlug: string }> }
9	) {
10	  const { studioSlug } = await params
11	  const ip = req.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') ?? 'unknown'
12	  const rl = await publicBookingReadRatelimit.limit(ip)
13	  if (!rl.success) return NextResponse.json({ error: 'Too many requests' }, { status: 429 })
14	
15	  const supabase = createPublicClient()
16	
17	  try {
18	    // Resolve studio id

20	      .from('studios')
21	      .select('id')
22	      .eq('slug', studioSlug)
23	      .maybeSingle()
24	
25	    if (!studio) return NextResponse.json({ data: [] })
26	
27	    const { data, error } = await supabase
28	      .from('style_tags')
29	      .select('*')
30	      .eq('studio_id', studio.id)
31	      .order('sort_order', { ascending: true })
32	
33	    if (error) {

content.text:
Pushed `db7c3d8`. 

**Root cause:** `GettingStartedCard` called `localStorage.getItem(...)` inside `useState`'s lazy initializer (line 72). That runs differently on server (returns `false`) vs client (returns `true` if dismissed). When the card returned `null` on the client but not on the server, the `RoleAwareHero` below shifted up into its slot → hydration mismatch.

**Fix:** Both server and first client render always show the card. A `useEffect` runs after mount and hides it if localStorage says dismissed. This keeps SSR output identical to initial client render.

**About the script-tag warning:** That's still `next-themes`' intentional inline theme-detection script. React 19 dev-mode noise only, not a bug. Ignore it.

Refresh `/dashboard` — the hydration error should be gone.

# Fix Two Dev Runtime Errors

## Context

After the minimal-strip refactor, `pnpm dev` throws two errors in the browser:

1. **CRITICAL — pino-pretty missing**
   `lib/logger.ts:11` instantiates pino with `transport: { target: 'pino-pretty' }` when `NODE_ENV === 'development'`. We deleted `pino-pretty` from devDependencies during the strip, so pino can't resolve the transport module — this crashes the logger at module-evaluation time. Any file that imports the logger (directly or transitively through `components/shared/PageError.tsx` → `app/error.tsx`) fails to render. This is the error blocking the app.

2. **COSMETIC — Script tag in React component**
   `<script>` is rendered inside RootLayout. Stack trace points to minified `V` / `J` functions inside `node_modules__pnpm_0dzjeft._.js`. That's `next-themes` — its `ThemeProvider` injects an inline `<script>` at render time to set the theme class before React hydrates (prevents flash). React 19 dev-mode now warns about client-rendered script tags. **This is expected next-themes behavior, runs correctly on SSR, and has no runtime impact.** The warning is dev-only noise. Rankora uses the same `next-themes@0.4.6` and works fine on Railway.

---

## The Fix

### Fix 1 — Remove `pino-pretty` transport from `lib/logger.ts`

**File:** [lib/logger.ts](lib/logger.ts)

Delete the `...(NODE_ENV === 'development' && { transport: { target: 'pino-pretty', ... } })` block. Production Railway already outputs JSON (correct behavior). Local `pnpm dev` will output raw JSON to the terminal — slightly less pretty, but zero dependencies and zero crashes.

If pretty output is wanted locally later, pipe the dev command through pino-pretty CLI:
```bash
pnpm dev 2>&1 | pnpm dlx pino-pretty
```

**Before:**
```ts
export const logger = pino({
  level: ...,
  // ...
  ...(process.env.NODE_ENV === 'development' && {
    transport: {
      target: 'pino-pretty',
      options: { colorize: true, translateTime: 'HH:MM:ss', ignore: 'pid,hostname' },
    },
  }),
})
```

**After:**
```ts
export const logger = pino({
  level: ...,
  // ...
  // (transport block removed — pino-pretty was removed from devDeps in minimal strip)
})
```

### Fix 2 — Leave script-tag warning alone (not a bug)

**File:** `app/layout.tsx` (line 56-60, `<ThemeProvider>` from next-themes)

No change. React 19's dev-mode warning about next-themes' intentional inline script is noise. It:
- Does NOT appear in production builds
- Does NOT affect theme switching or rendering
- Will be silenced by a future next-themes update (already tracked upstream)

**Do NOT:**
- Switch to `scriptProps` workaround — adds complexity, no benefit
- Drop next-themes — breaks dark mode everywhere
- Upgrade next-themes past 0.4.6 — no newer version available as of plan date

**If the warning is distracting:** the browser console has a "Filter" box — type `Script` to hide these warnings during dev.

---

## Verification

1. Edit `lib/logger.ts` — remove the transport block
2. Refresh `http://localhost:3100/login` — page renders without crash, no pino-pretty error
3. Open DevTools Console — the `<script>` warning may still appear (expected, ignore)
4. Server terminal shows raw JSON log output instead of formatted (acceptable for minimal dev)

---

## Out of Scope

- Adding pino-pretty back as devDep (not worth the dependency; pipe-based alternative exists)
- Fixing next-themes script warning (cosmetic, upstream issue, no runtime effect)
- Any other error-boundary restructuring

content.text:
Pushed `e83a7c1`.

**Root cause:** `z.coerce.boolean()` in `/api/clients/route.ts:43` was a footgun — it uses JavaScript's `Boolean()`, so `Boolean("false") === true`. Client sent `archived=false` → Zod turned it into `true` → query filtered for archived-only clients → returned `[]` → Jessica vanished right after mount.

**Fixed:**
- `archived`: now accepts `'true' | 'false' | 'any'` as a string enum, with correct 3-state filter logic
- `vip`, `inactive`, `no_show`: now use a strict `'true' | 'false'` transformer that returns real booleans (or `undefined` if missing)

Refresh `/clients` — Jessica should now stay on the page. The same class of bug can hit any route using `z.coerce.boolean()` on query params; I can sweep for it if you want, but this one was the visible one.

# InkOS Global UI Elevation Ladder — Premium SaaS Depth

## Context

User feedback: *"all same background in whole SaaS... lets become different somewhere... more amazing and according UI UX rules and brand consistency... more Interesting addictive"*

Screenshot + token audit confirms the core issue:

| Region | Current token | Current color |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar | `--sidebar` | `#F7F7F5` (bone) |
| Top bar (sticky header) | `bg-background/80 backdrop-blur` | ~white translucent over bone |
| Content area (`main` + `PageShell`) | `--color-page-bg` | `oklch(97.5% 0.003 85)` (bone) |
| Cards / surface-1 | `--color-surface-1` | `#FFFFFF` (white) |

**The three chrome regions (sidebar / top bar / content) are the exact same tone.** There is no visual separation between the nav chrome and the content "canvas", so the UI feels flat and monotone. Premium SaaS apps (Linear, Attio, Superhuman, Vercel, Raycast) solve this with a deliberate elevation ladder that recedes the chrome and pushes the content forward — or vice-versa. InkOS currently has no ladder at all.

The fix is **a deliberate 4-layer elevation ladder** using warm stone-hue tones exclusively (Brand Book v1.0 — Bone/Rust/Stone/Onyx). No new hues, no gimmicks, no texture overlays — just disciplined tonal separation plus a few micro-accents that are already in the codebase.

---

## The Ladder (Option A — Recessed Chrome)

This is the pattern used by Linear, Superhuman, Attio. Chrome sits slightly recessed, content sits forward, cards float on top.

### Light mode

| Layer | Z-order | Token | New value | Visible as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0 — Chrome (sidebar)** | Recessed | `--sidebar` + `--sidebar-background` | `oklch(95.5% 0.004 85)` | Deeper warm bone — ~2% darker than content canvas. Feels "behind" the content. |
| **L0a — Chrome (top bar)** | Recessed | `AppHeader` `<header>` class | `bg-[var(--color-header-bg)]/85 backdrop-blur-md` + stronger `border-b` | Pure white translucent with clearer hairline border when content scrolls underneath. |
| **L1 — Canvas (content area)** | Base | `--color-page-bg` | `oklch(97.5% 0.003 85)` (unchanged — bone) | Main work surface. |
| **L2 — Cards / surface-1** | Elevated | `--color-surface-1` | `oklch(100% 0 0)` (unchanged — pure white) | Floating surfaces pop against bone canvas. |
| **Separators** | — | `--sidebar-border`, `--color-border` | `oklch(91% 0.005 85)` | Warm hairline, slightly stronger than current so the sidebar→content seam is visible without being harsh. |

### Dark mode

| Layer | Token | New value |
|---|---|---|
| L0 — Sidebar | `--sidebar` | `oklch(11% 0.006 85)` — deeper onyx (3% darker than page-bg) |
| L0a — Top bar | `--color-header-bg` | `oklch(13% 0.006 85 / 0.85)` |
| L1 — Canvas | `--color-page-bg` | `oklch(14% 0.005 85)` (unchanged) |
| L2 — Cards / surface-1 | `--color-surface-1` | `oklch(20% 0.007 85)` (unchanged) |
| Separators | `--sidebar-border`, `--color-border` | `oklch(22% 0.008 85)` |

---

## Secondary Accents (already in the codebase — verify they render)

These are micro-touches from the prior commits that complete the "premium" feel. No new code; just verify they show up once the ladder lands.

1. **PageShell warm radial highlight** (added in prior commit) — soft top-right bone→warm-white highlight, barely-there rust whisper bottom-left. Adds tonal drift across the canvas.
2. **PageHeader rust hairline** — 40px fading rust stripe 16px below every page title.
3. **Bumped card shadows** — `--shadow-card` / `--shadow-card-hover` alpha bumped so cards lift visibly against L1.
4. **Sidebar icons sharper** — full sidebar-foreground color, strokeWidth 2.25, 17px.

---

## Files to Modify (minimal — tokens only for the ladder)

### 1. `app/globals.css` — update elevation tokens

Light mode block (around line 180-212):
```css
/* Sidebar — L0 recessed chrome */
--sidebar:                       oklch(95.5% 0.004 85);  /* was #F7F7F5 */
--sidebar-background:            oklch(95.5% 0.004 85);  /* was #F7F7F5 */
--sidebar-foreground:            #0F0F0F;                /* unchanged */
--sidebar-border:                oklch(91% 0.005 85);    /* was oklch(89% 0.002 60) */
/* ...other sidebar tokens unchanged... */

/* Global border — tuned to read on bone canvas without being harsh */

/* Page surfaces — already warm (hue 85) — only minor tweaks */

--color-header-bg:               oklch(100% 0 0);        /* unchanged — L0a */
--color-surface-1:               oklch(100% 0 0);        /* unchanged — L2 */
```

Dark mode block (around line 948-990):

### 2. `components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx` — strengthen top-bar border

# InkOS Global UI Elevation Ladder — Premium SaaS Depth

## Context

User feedback: *"all same background in whole SaaS... lets become different somewhere... more amazing and according UI UX rules and brand consistency... more Interesting addictive"*

Screenshot + token audit confirms the core issue:

| Region | Current token | Current color |
|---|---|---|
| Sidebar | `--sidebar` | `#F7F7F5` (bone) |
| Top bar (sticky header) | `bg-background/80 backdrop-blur` | ~white translucent over bone |
| Content area (`main` + `PageShell`) | `--color-page-bg` | `oklch(97.5% 0.003 85)` (bone) |
| Cards / surface-1 | `--color-surface-1` | `#FFFFFF` (white) |

**The three chrome regions (sidebar / top bar / content) are the exact same tone.** There is no visual separation between the nav chrome and the content "canvas", so the UI feels flat and monotone. Premium SaaS apps (Linear, Attio, Superhuman, Vercel, Raycast) solve this with a deliberate elevation ladder that recedes the chrome and pushes the content forward — or vice-versa. InkOS currently has no ladder at all.

The fix is **a deliberate 4-layer elevation ladder** using warm stone-hue tones exclusively (Brand Book v1.0 — Bone/Rust/Stone/Onyx). No new hues, no gimmicks, no texture overlays — just disciplined tonal separation plus a few micro-accents that are already in the codebase.

---

## The Ladder (Option A — Recessed Chrome)

This is the pattern used by Linear, Superhuman, Attio. Chrome sits slightly recessed, content sits forward, cards float on top.

### Light mode

| Layer | Z-order | Token | New value | Visible as |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **L0 — Chrome (sidebar)** | Recessed | `--sidebar` + `--sidebar-background` | `oklch(95.5% 0.004 85)` | Deeper warm bone — ~2% darker than content canvas. Feels "behind" the content. |
| **L0a — Chrome (top bar)** | Recessed | `AppHeader` `<header>` class | `bg-[var(--color-header-bg)]/85 backdrop-blur-md` + stronger `border-b` | Pure white translucent with clearer hairline border when content scrolls underneath. |
| **L1 — Canvas (content area)** | Base | `--color-page-bg` | `oklch(97.5% 0.003 85)` (unchanged — bone) | Main work surface. |
| **L2 — Cards / surface-1** | Elevated | `--color-surface-1` | `oklch(100% 0 0)` (unchanged — pure white) | Floating surfaces pop against bone canvas. |
| **Separators** | — | `--sidebar-border`, `--color-border` | `oklch(91% 0.005 85)` | Warm hairline, slightly stronger than current so the sidebar→content seam is visible without being harsh. |

### Dark mode

| Layer | Token | New value |
|---|---|---|
| L0 — Sidebar | `--sidebar` | `oklch(11% 0.006 85)` — deeper onyx (3% darker than page-bg) |
| L0a — Top bar | `--color-header-bg` | `oklch(13% 0.006 85 / 0.85)` |
| L1 — Canvas | `--color-page-bg` | `oklch(14% 0.005 85)` (unchanged) |
| L2 — Cards / surface-1 | `--color-surface-1` | `oklch(20% 0.007 85)` (unchanged) |
| Separators | `--sidebar-border`, `--color-border` | `oklch(22% 0.008 85)` |

---

## Secondary Accents (already in the codebase — verify they render)

These are micro-touches from the prior commits that complete the "premium" feel. No new code; just verify they show up once the ladder lands.

1. **PageShell warm radial highlight** (added in prior commit) — soft top-right bone→warm-white highlight, barely-there rust whisper bottom-left. Adds tonal drift across the canvas.
2. **PageHeader rust hairline** — 40px fading rust stripe 16px below every page title.
3. **Bumped card shadows** — `--shadow-card` / `--shadow-card-hover` alpha bumped so cards lift visibly against L1.
4. **Sidebar icons sharper** — full sidebar-foreground color, strokeWidth 2.25, 17px.

---

## Files to Modify (minimal — tokens only for the ladder)

### 1. `app/globals.css` — update elevation tokens

Light mode block (around line 180-212):
```css
/* Sidebar — L0 recessed chrome */
--sidebar:                       oklch(95.5% 0.004 85);  /* was #F7F7F5 */
--sidebar-background:            oklch(95.5% 0.004 85);  /* was #F7F7F5 */
--sidebar-foreground:            #0F0F0F;                /* unchanged */
--sidebar-border:                oklch(91% 0.005 85);    /* was oklch(89% 0.002 60) */
/* ...other sidebar tokens unchanged... */

/* Global border — tuned to read on bone canvas without being harsh */
--color-border:                  oklch(91% 0.005 85);   /* was oklch(89% 0.002 60) */
--color-input:                   oklch(91% 0.005 85);   /* was oklch(89% 0.002 60) */

/* Page surfaces — already warm (hue 85) — only minor tweaks */
--color-page-bg:                 oklch(97.5% 0.003 85);  /* unchanged — L1 canvas */
--color-header-bg:               oklch(100% 0 0);        /* unchanged — L0a */
--color-surface-1:               oklch(100% 0 0);        /* unchanged — L2 */
```

Dark mode block (around line 948-990):
```css
--color-border:                  oklch(22% 0.008 85);
--color-input:                   oklch(20% 0.007 85);
--color-page-bg:                 oklch(14% 0.005 85);    /* unchanged */
--color-header-bg:               oklch(13% 0.006 85 / 0.85);
--sidebar:                       oklch(11% 0.006 85);    /* was 17% — deeper now */
--sidebar-background:            oklch(11% 0.006 85);
--sidebar-border:                oklch(22% 0.008 85);
```

### 2. `components/app/sidebar/AppHeader.tsx` — strengthen top-bar border

Line 244 currently:
```tsx
<header className="sticky top-0 z-40 flex h-14 ... border-b border-border/60 bg-background/80 px-4 backdrop-blur-md supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-background/70">
```

Change to:
```tsx
<header className="sticky top-0 z-40 flex h-14 ... border-b border-border bg-[var(--color-header-bg)]/85 px-4 backdrop-blur-md supports-[backdrop-filter]:bg-[var(--color-header-bg)]/75">
```

Swaps: border opacity /60 → full (tuned via new warm token), and uses `--color-header-bg` token instead of `--background` so the header reads as pure white over the (now deeper) sidebar + bone content.

### 3. `components/app/sidebar/AppSidebar.tsx` — right-edge vertical gradient accent (optional brand flourish)

Add a 1px rust-tinted gradient on the sidebar's right edge so the seam between L0 and L1 gets a subtle brand signature. Pure CSS, no layout impact:
```tsx
<Sidebar className="before:pointer-events-none before:absolute before:right-0 before:top-0 before:h-full before:w-px before:bg-[linear-gradient(to_bottom,_transparent_0%,_oklch(58%_0.16_35/_0.12)_40%,_oklch(58%_0.16_35/_0.12)_60%,_transparent_100%)]">
```

Effect: barely-visible rust hairline down the center of the sidebar's right edge. Fades at top/bottom. Zero visual noise, strong brand signal in peripheral vision.

---

## What is NOT changing

- No new hues (everything stays on hue 85 + rust 35 + onyx)
- No texture/grain/noise overlays (can do later if user asks; risks being gimmicky)
- No per-page-type tonal variants (Studio/Operations/Growth) — premature, adds surface area without proven UX benefit
- No typography changes
- No spacing / layout / component-architecture changes

---

## Verification

1. `pnpm typecheck` — must pass (CSS changes don't affect TS; just a sanity check nothing else regressed)
2. `pnpm build` — must succeed
3. Manual walkthrough at `localhost:3100`:
   - **Light mode**: sidebar clearly reads as deeper warm bone than the content canvas. Top bar reads as white over both. Cards float visibly on the canvas.
   - **Dark mode**: sidebar clearly reads as deeper onyx than content. Same ladder preserved in inverse.
   - Sidebar→content seam is visible (hairline), not harsh.
   - Rust edge accent barely visible but adds warmth on hover focus.
   - No ugly color banding, no sudden tonal jumps.
4. Checked pages: `/today` (has its own hero), `/clients` (table density), `/inventory` (tabs + toolbar), `/settings` (form density), `/messages` (full-height split). All four must look improved and none must look worse.

---

## Agent Routing (per CLAUDE.md roster)

| Step | Agent | Task |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **koda** (Pod A) | Apply the token changes to `app/globals.css` for both light + dark blocks. Update `AppHeader.tsx:244` per spec. Add the optional sidebar right-edge gradient to `AppSidebar.tsx`. Commit: `style(brand): 4-layer elevation ladder — recessed chrome, floating cards, rust edge accent`. Push. |
| 2 | **sage** (Code Review) | Verify no tokens with hue 264 / 60 residuals reintroduced. Verify no `bg-[#...]` hex bypass of tokens. Verify dark mode parity. Run `pnpm typecheck` + `pnpm build`. Sign off. |
| 3 | **vega** (Design Lead) | Walk through /today, /clients, /inventory, /settings, /messages in both light + dark. Confirm elevation ladder reads correctly and rust edge accent is tasteful. Final sign-off. |

Single sprint. Out-of-scope for this plan: the two pre-existing TS errors in `ClientDrawer.tsx` + `clients/page.tsx` (tracked separately).

Author: Boldteq <saas@boldteq.com>

    fix(breadcrumbs): include non-root section segments in trail
    
    On routes that are NOT prefixed by the virtual root (i.e. everything
    except /admin/*), buildTrail() was slicing off the first segment
    because rootSegments.length = 1 for rootHref="/dashboard". Result:
    - /inbox      → segments=['inbox'], relative=[], trail=[Dashboard]
    - /clients    → segments=['clients'], relative=[], trail=[Dashboard]
    - /artists/id → relative=['id'], trail=[Dashboard, Id]
    
    Fix: only slice when path actually starts with rootHref. For virtual
    roots, keep all segments and accumulate built from '' (not from
    rootHref). This makes `/inbox` render [Dashboard > Inbox] correctly,
    and nested routes like `/settings/studio/services` render the full
    4-crumb trail.
    
    Also restores AppSidebar StudioSwitcher + BookingLinkWidget imports

Pushed `ac66938`.

**What changed on `/clients`:**

Before (two competing heading rows):
```
Clients                                       [rust hairline]
Manage client profiles, history, and notes.
─────────────────────────────────────────
Clients                                       [+ New client]
1 of 1 client
[All clients] [VIPs] [New this month] ...
```

After (single heading + compact toolbar):
```
Clients                                       [rust hairline]
Manage client profiles, history, and notes.
─────────────────────────────────────────
[All clients ▼] [VIPs] [New this month]   1 of 1 clients  [+ New client]
[search] [tags] [VIP] ...                                 [Columns]
[table]
```

**UX rules applied:**
- **One heading per page** — PageHeader owns the title, serif font, description, and rust hairline signature
- **Result count** now sits inline with the primary-action toolbar as a small muted `tabular-nums` text (standard pattern in Linear/Attio/Superhuman), not as a heading subtitle
- **Primary CTA** (`+ New client`) compacted to `size="sm"` and placed on the right of the filter row (same visual weight as `+ New view`)
- **Inactive badge** kept but shrunk to a smaller pill so it reads as metadata, not a headline

Reload `/clients` — only one "Clients" heading, and the page breathes.

Also swept: `InventoryHub`, `PaymentsPageClient`, `AppointmentsPageClient` — none had duplicate h1s. Only `/clients` was affected.
